context: A uni intern interviews a manager about product testing
purpose: Teach: キャンセル/器具/儲かる/スクリプト/ゲート/実例/使い勝手/成り立た

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 新製品の器具、使い勝手はどう確かめるんですか。
lines.en: How do you test whether new equipment actually works well for people?
lines.style: Genuine curiosity, formal but not stiff. Leans forward slightly on the question. Respectful of her expertise without self-consciousness about asking.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 実例を集めて、スクリプト化したテストを通します。
lines.en: We collect real-world data and run it through standardized test cases.
lines.style: Clear and matter-of-fact, taking his question seriously. Matter-of-fact pacing, slight lift at the end showing she's inviting follow-up.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: コストが成り立たないと、儲かる事業にならないですよね。
lines.en: But if the costs don't work out, you can't actually make money off it, can you?
lines.style: Thoughtful probe, not challenging. He's thinking out loud, checking his logic. Slight hesitation before 'make money' — testing the idea as he says it.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: はい。ゲート審査に通過した案件だけ、量産化します。
lines.en: Right. We only move projects into full production if they pass the gate review.
lines.style: Affirmative and straightforward. Light emphasis on 'only' — establishing the checkpoint clearly. Steady, explanatory tone without condescension.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: キャンセル率の許容範囲、決まってますか。
lines.en: Is there a specific threshold for how many cancellations are acceptable?
lines.style: Following thread naturally. Conversational energy has built — he's engaging deeper. Slight uptick in pace, still respectful, genuinely interested in the metrics.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 各部署で目安があります。
lines.en: Each department has its own benchmarks.
lines.style: Warm permission to keep asking. Brief answer that opens rather than closes — soft, approachable. The tone of someone who sees his questions are genuine and worthwhile.
